scope: Crustaceans, chelicerates and fish; quantitative tidal/diel evidence, original open-data audit; no pooled effect estimated.
method: Primary articles, publisher supplements, public repository metadata and original author code inspected. Numeric values retained on their original scales. Model-selection statistics are not converted to effect sizes. Direct open downloads were attempted; Anubis-blocked Dryad data were not acquired.

records.title: Environmental variables driving horseshoe crab spawning behavior in a microtidal lagoon in Florida
records.authors: Heres B, Abeels H, Shea C, Crowley-McIntyre CE
records.study_units: Two fixed shorelines within one northern Indian River Lagoon coast; daily surveys, not independent coast replicates.
records.observations: 2019-02-02 to 2019-04-30; highest daytime tide only; count of spawning horseshoe crabs.

quantitative.estimand: Conditional log expected count/rate change per +1 metre water height
quantitative.model: Negative binomial log-link, site fixed covariate, offset log(transect length)

quantitative.locator: Table 3, Global Interaction model, Tide row
quantitative.estimand: Same water-height slope with additional wind-by-onshore interaction

raw_data.timezone: not specified in CSV; not independently resolved

quality_notes: Methods state 162 measured USGS gauge heights, 8 NOAA predictions, and 3 omitted surveys. The CSV has 8 missing USGS values; three rows have missing Onshore values. Tide is complete, combining gauge and predicted values.

Transect length in paper: Kelly 213 m, Parrish 597 m. The CSV-derived CpM uses TotalCrabs/596 for all 34 positive Kelly rows and TotalCrabs/597 for all 31 positive Parrish rows. This discrepancy is observed, not resolved; use raw counts and verify documented offsets before reproducing model.
Water height is wind-driven water level in a microtidal lagoon, not a clean periodic tide phase treatment.
Day-only sampling at the predicted highest daytime tide cannot identify diel effects or a tide-by-diel interaction. Preserve as tide-only null/context evidence.
Data availability text claims both raw data and R script; only S1 CSV was found/retrieved in the inspected supplement list, not a verified R script.

records.title: Multi-scale temporal patterns in fish presence in a high-velocity tidal channel
records.taxon: Unidentified mixed fish assemblage; individuals tracked acoustically, species not separable
records.study_units: One bottom-mounted acoustic site, one independent coast; two years do not create two studies.
records.observations: Hourly acoustic fish passage counts, July 15 2013 to July 28 2015; paper says 582 days with observed acoustic data.

quantitative.result: Winter/spring highest counts at ebb/low slack near dawn/dusk; summer/fall higher night counts and broader ebb/low/flood distribution.
quantitative.reason: Published wavelet/visual seasonal pattern, no reported common conditional coefficient with sampling variance.

raw_data.known_schema: Repository description says two-year hourly fish-count series with corresponding tidal and diel stages; exact columns not inspected.
raw_data.zero_vs_missing: UNVERIFIED: original missing/gap-fill flags not inspected
raw_data.download_failures: Public file links returned HTTP 403 to web/urllib; alternate fetch showed Anubis 'Validating' screen. API whole-dataset download returned 401. Public landing page accessible in browser, no download click or challenge action; stopped when parent instructed.

quality_notes: Tidal phase was reconstructed from observed fish swimming directions in the 4D acoustic data, then validated against several measured ADCP spans. The nearest external tide station was judged inaccurate.

Directions and counts are different properties of the acoustic detections but not fully independent data streams. Any independent tidal-predictor analysis needs explicit provenance/sensitivity treatment.

For wavelet analysis, 20 gaps (2 h to 29.5 d) were filled using fitted 0.5, 1.0, 14.7, 27.6, 182 and 365-day harmonics plus noise. Those synthetic values must be excluded from predictive validation; original/filled flags unverified.
Only individually resolved fish were counted. Schools could not be reliably distinguished from entrained air and were removed; seasonal schooling may contribute to apparent diel count patterns.
Counts reflect passage/detection at sampled depth, not confirmed feeding, individual behavioral state, or species-level temporal niches.
Do not fit/claim a raw-data result until original CSV/README bytes are obtained and audited.

records.title: Crabs ride the tide: incoming tides promote foraging of Giant Mud Crab (Scylla serrata)
records.authors: Hewitt DE, Johnson DD, Suthers IM, Taylor MD
records.study_units: 18 tagged adults; Table 1 contains 13 analyzed crabs, one creek/estuary coast; repeated 15-min positions/acceleration.
records.endpoint: HMM-inferred foraging/inactivity from step length, turning angle and acceleration.

quantitative.estimand: stationary foraging probability at low versus high tide

quantitative.locator: Results covariate selection; Supplementary Table S2
quantitative.result: tide height by change in height interaction selected; hour, water temperature and habitat removed.
quantitative.not_effect_size: AIC selection does not estimate an absence/equivalence effect.

raw_data.project: NSW DPI Coastal and Estuarine Fish Tracking (CEFT)
raw_data.supplement_status: discovered; PMC download reached browser-check page, not acquired

quality_notes: HMM state inference and covariate effects are jointly fitted. Viterbi activity labels made by the tide-conditioned model are not independent outcomes for testing whether tide predicts behavior. Refit observation-only states or use raw acceleration with a prespecified external tide source for a common predictive protocol.
Low/incoming-tide stationarity curves are model-derived; confidence bands in Fig 5 do not supply the covariance necessary for the low/high ratio SE.
Individual random-mixture components were removed by model selection; that does not turn 15-min observations into independent crabs.
Authors report ~12-h residual autocorrelation and say adding hour did not improve it; no support for a selected diel covariate is not a precise null effect.
Hyperbolic positioning algorithm was proprietary at publication; raw IMOS detections may not alone reproduce processed locations.

records.title: Vertical Movements of Juvenile Sablefish in Coastal Southeast Alaska
records.authors: Coutré KM, Beaudreau AH, Courtney D, Mueter FJ, Malecha PW, Rutecki TL
records.study_units: 13 tagged, six analyzed; one bay; two receivers do not create independent coasts.
records.observations: October 5–November 14, 2003; binary excursion in a 10-min detection interval when at least one depth observation <19 m.

quantitative.scale: mean excursion fraction across 6 fish; paper prints mean ± 2 SE
quantitative.se_derivation: Reported ±2SE divided by 2; means/SE rounded in publication.
quantitative.reason: Same fish contribute all conditions; covariance and cell-specific exposure unavailable; tidal and diel marginals are not tidal-by-diel cells.

quantitative.locator: Table 3, p.166, Date + Diel + Tide row
quantitative.scale: conditional logit coefficients, reference dawn and ebb

quantitative.not_effect_size: Selection favors date+diel; AIC is not a comparable effect.
Not six independent studies or a binomial prevalence estimate of ecological tidal control.

raw_data.status: not located as openly downloadable files
raw_data.primary_source: NOAA 2003 acoustic telemetry data described in paper
raw_data.tidal_source: Neva Strait predictions from University of South Carolina tide predictor
raw_data.solar_source: US Naval Observatory Sitka nautical dawn/sunrise/sunset/nautical dusk

quality_notes: Published tidal marginal means are nearly identical, providing a descriptive null with uncertainty but not an adjusted tidal contrast SE.
Fish identity random intercept included in group GLMM; many bins are repeated measures.
Some depth changes could be horizontal movements over bathymetry; foraging is an interpretation, not a directly observed state.
Raw data search did not produce a verified repository, supplementary CSV or covariance matrix.

records.title: Tidal-diel patterns in feeding and abundance of armed snook Centropomus armatus from macrotidal mangrove creeks of the tropical eastern Pacific Ocean
records.authors: Pülmanns N, Castellanos-Galindo GA, Krumme U
records.study_units: Four Estero Luisico mangrove creeks in one Bahía Málaga coastal system; one-year 2009–2010 sampling.

contents_advertised: Methods M1 final fish abundance LMM
Methods M2 final stomach fullness LMM
Fig S1 stomach-fullness classes of 282 stomachs across eight tide/diel/salinity combinations
Table S1 prey composition from 296 stomachs
Table S2 sampling scheme of four creeks, December 2009 to November 2010
data_lead.status: publisher supporting-information metadata inspected; file not retrieved and model coefficients not verified

records.findings_at_abstract_level: Abundance and stomach fullness highest neap-night; abundance lowest spring-day; stomach fullness lowest neap-day. Daily consumption higher spring than neap.
quality_notes: No numeric contrast plus variance extracted; not meta-ready.
Spring/neap contrast is fortnightly tidal-amplitude regime, distinct from within-day tide stage.
Stomach fullness, catch abundance, and daily consumption are separate endpoints.
Do not infer cell counts from 282 or 296 stomach totals; denominator/effort table remains needed.

records.title: From non-tidal to tidal environments: movement behaviour of Chinese mitten crabs on downstream spawning migration
records.authors: Keirsebelik H, Verhelst P, D'hondt B, Schoelynck J
records.study_units: 34 tagged; 33 detected/analyzed; six accelerometer tags. One connected river-estuary/coast crossing national boundary; 90,107 detections are repeated observations.

quantitative.locator: Results, Circadian and circatidal patterns in acceleration / Fig 6

records.model: Log acceleration LME, nested receiver-within-tag random effects and corAR1; full tidal model circadian phase × tidal phase + sex, backward AIC; final tidal model retains tidal phase only.

raw_data.status: repository metadata confirmed; raw files not retrieved

quality_notes: Reported condition means with CI are correlated model predictions; do not construct independent-means log ratios without covariance.
No circadian term retained in tidal zone is model-selection evidence, not a precise null contrast.
Belgian-only subset could be relevant outside Netherlands if raw data are obtained; entire paper cannot be labeled wholly outside Netherlands.
Diel labels were derived from suncalc; twilight includes astronomical dawn/dusk; water levels are independent 10-min station data/interpolation.
Tidal arrival/departure count n=314 and overall diel count n=827 are repeated events, not independent crab counts.

conclusion.next_step: Acquire/inspect original fish CSV/README through authorized access and retain raw missing/effort flags; independently freeze analysis before any outcome-derived tuning. No effect calculation performed.
